privacy.metaDescription: How Family Tree handles account data, tree records, cookies, and your choices.
privacy.title: Privacy policy
privacy.lead: This policy explains what we collect when you use Family Tree, why we need it, and the choices you have. It is written for a private family-tree product — not as legal advice for every jurisdiction.

scope.title: What this covers
scope.body: It applies to the Family Tree web app and the APIs that power signed-in dashboards. Marketing pages may use only technical logs needed to serve the site.

accounts.title: Accounts
accounts.body: When you sign in we process credentials and profile fields needed to authenticate you, apply roles, and show the right trees. Keep your password private; administrators may manage accounts according to your organisation’s rules.

data.title: Family data you enter
data.body: People, marriages, photos, and related notes stay inside the trees you can access. That content is treated as private family records: it is not sold, and it is not used for advertising.

cookies.title: Cookies and local storage
cookies.body: We use essential storage for sign-in sessions, theme preference, locale, and a one-time splash flag. We do not load third-party advertising trackers on the product surfaces.

sharing.title: Sharing
sharing.body: Data is shared with infrastructure providers that host the app and API only as needed to run the service, or when the law requires disclosure. Tree members see what their permissions allow.

rights.title: Your choices
rights.body: You can update profile details you control, ask an administrator to correct or remove records you should not keep, and sign out to end the local session. Export features may let you take a copy of tree data you are allowed to view.

contact.title: Questions
contact.body: If you need a privacy request for a hosted deployment, contact the operator who runs your Family Tree instance — they control the data store and retention window.

terms.metaDescription: Terms for using Family Tree dashboards, private trees, and related APIs.
terms.title: Terms of use
terms.lead: By signing in or using Family Tree you agree to these terms. Operators of a self-hosted or managed instance may add their own organisational rules on top.

acceptance.title: Agreement
acceptance.body: If you do not agree, do not use the service. Continued use after a published change means you accept the updated terms.

service.title: The service
service.body: Family Tree helps authorised users maintain private pedigrees, relationships, and exports. Features may change as the product evolves.

accounts.title: Accounts and access
accounts.body: You are responsible for activity under your credentials. Do not share passwords or attempt to access trees or admin tools without permission. Roles and permissions define what each account may view or edit.

content.title: Your content
content.body: You (or your organisation) retain rights to the family data you upload. You must have a lawful basis to store personal information about relatives, and you must not upload unlawful or harmful material.

availability.title: Availability
availability.body: We aim for reliable uptime but do not guarantee uninterrupted access. Backups and maintenance windows depend on how the instance is operated.

liability.title: Limitation
liability.body: The software is provided as-is for genealogy and record-keeping. To the extent allowed by law, operators are not liable for indirect damages arising from use or downtime. Keep your own exports of critical records.

changes.title: Changes
changes.body: These terms may be updated. The “Last updated” date on this page will change when material edits ship.

help.title: Guide
help.lead: How the dashboard and family-tree workspace fit together. Skim a section, or jump below — you can flesh these notes out later.

sections.appLead: Signed-in navigation, trees list, profile, tickets, and admin tools when your role allows.
sections.pedigreeLead: Everything inside an open tree: people, marriages, paths, timeline, Excel, and exports.

dashboard.title: Home / dashboard
dashboard.body: The welcome page summarises what you can do. Open Family trees from the sidebar to start working; admin links (Users, Roles) appear only if your permissions allow.

profile.title: My profile
profile.body: See username, email, phone, role, and account type. Sub-pages cover permissions (read-only list), password change, and active sessions you can revoke.

trees.title: Family trees list
trees.body: Create a new private tree or open an existing one. Each tree is a tenant boundary — people and marriages never leak across trees.

treeSettings.title: Tree settings
treeSettings.body: From a tree’s settings page rename the tree, manage members, and adjust who can view or edit. Access is per tree, not global.

tickets.title: Support tickets
tickets.body: Open a ticket for account or product issues. Optionally link a family tree. Staff with ticket permissions can reply and change status.

users.title: Users (admin)
users.body: List, create, and edit accounts: full name, username, optional email and phone (with country code), role, account type, password reset, and session revoke.

roles.title: Roles & permissions (admin)
roles.body: Roles bundle named permissions. Assign a role to a user so they only see the menus and tree actions they are allowed to use.

limits.title: Free account limits
limits.body: Free accounts may hit quotas on trees, people, or marriages. Paid (or admin-granted) accounts lift those caps. The app shows a notice when a free limit blocks an action.

canvas.title: Canvas basics
canvas.body: Pan by dragging the background and zoom with the wheel or pinch. The graph shows people and marriage links. Empty trees prompt you to add the first person.

search.title: Search
search.body: Use the header search to find people by name. Picking a result focuses and frames that person on the canvas.

people.title: People
people.body: Add a person from the header or tools menu. Open a person to edit names, gender, dates, places, notes, photo, and parent links. Delete carefully — linked marriages may block removal.

marriages.title: Marriages
marriages.body: Add a marriage between two people (needs at least two persons). Record marriage or divorce dates. Marriages appear as links on the graph.

parents.title: Parents & children
parents.body: On a person, attach parents with a type: biological, adoptive, or step. Children show under the right marriage or parent pair when data allows.

fold.title: Fold / expand branches
fold.body: Collapse busy branches to reduce clutter, then expand again from the chip in the header. Branch preview can focus a subtree; exit returns to the full tree.

timeline.title: Timeline by year
timeline.body: Slide or pick a year to see who was alive (or present) at that time. Useful for historical snapshots of the same tree.

relations.title: Find relation (paths)
relations.body: From a person, choose Find relation and pick another person. The closest path loads first. A moment later alternative routes may appear — switch among them and choose full / all / active view to control highlighting.

birthdays.title: Birthday calendar
birthdays.body: Open the calendar tool to see upcoming birthdays from people who have a birth date you are allowed to view. Selecting a day jumps to that person.

excel.title: Excel sample, import, export
excel.body: Download a sample workbook, import with a preview of what will change, or export the whole tree. Large imports may take a few seconds — wait for the preview confirm step.

export.title: Image, PDF, lineage card
export.body: Export the visible tree as image or PDF, or generate a lineage / info card for a selected person. Use fit view first if you want the full graph in frame.

viewTools.title: Fit, tidy, fullscreen
viewTools.body: Fit view frames everyone. Tidy layout re-spaces nodes. Fullscreen hides chrome for a larger canvas — exit with the same control or Escape where supported.

treeTicket.title: Ticket from this tree
treeTicket.body: From the tools menu you can open a support ticket already linked to the current tree so staff see the right context.

u1.title: Email and phone on users
u1.body: Signup contact fields appear in user list, detail, and edit (with country code on create/edit).

u2.title: Alternative relation paths
u2.body: After the closest path, the pedigree loads other diverse kinship routes.

u3.title: Excel workflows
u3.body: Sample, preview, import, and export for whole trees.

u4.title: In-app guide
u4.body: Help icon on the dashboard and pedigree explains each area and recent updates.
